blocks.text: This article provides information on configuring and managing Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts using APIs. All APIs are rate limited. To learn more, see API Rate Limit Summary.
Before configuring and managing AWS accounts, make sure you've identified the access token required for authorization.

blocks.item: Send a POST request to the following endpoint:
/publicCloudInfo
Include the request headers to provide information about the request context:
Content Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Use the following JSON payload to create an AWS account and provide the following information:
publicCloudInfo:
(Required) name (String): The name of the AWS account.
accountDetails:
(Required) awsAccountId (String): The AWS account ID where workloads are deployed. The ID must be non-null, non-empty, and unique, and contain 12 digits.
(Required) awsRoleName (String): The AWS trusting role in your account. The name must be non-null, non-empty, and 64 characters or fewer in length.
accountGroups:
id (Integer): An ID that uniquely identifies an entity.
cloudType (String): The cloud type. The default value is AWS.
externalId (String): A unique external ID for the AWS account.
(Required) supportedRegions: Regions supported by the Zscaler Tag Discovery Service.
id (Integer): The unique ID of the supported region.
Creating an AWS Account

{ "name": "aws-account-1", "cloudType": "AWS", // optional "externalId": "daba767765f2670722c4d68e8f81bf90", // optional "accountDetails": { "awsAccountId": "674109010822", "awsRoleName": "role1" }, "supportedRegions": [ { "id": 456414 } ], // optional "accountGroups": [ { "id": 1090178 } ] }

blocks.text: A successful response returns code 201, meaning the AWS account is created. To learn more, see API Response Codes and Error Messages.

blocks.heading: Getting Details for All AWS Accounts

blocks.item: To get details for all AWS accounts, send a GET request to the following endpoint:
/publicCloudInfo
This API supports pagination. To get a paginated response, send a GET request to the following endpoint:
/publicCloudInfo?page=1&pagesize=2

blocks.heading: Getting Details of a Specific AWS Account

blocks.text: To get details for a particular AWS Account:

blocks.item: Send a GET request to the following endpoint:
/publicCloudInfo/{id}
Provide the unique ID of the AWS account in the request endpoint.
For example:
/publicCloudInfo/100

blocks.text: A successful response returns code 200. To learn more, see API Response Codes and Error Messages.
To update a specific AWS account:

blocks.item: Provide the updated JSON payload from the Creating an AWS Account section and send a PUT request to the following endpoint:
/publicCloudInfo/{id}
Provide the unique ID of the AWS account, account groups, and region in the request payload.

blocks.text: A successful response returns code 204. To learn more, see API Response Codes and Error Messages.

blocks.item: Send a DELETE request to the following endpoint:
/publicCloudInfo/{id}
Provide the unique ID of the AWS account in the request endpoint.
For example:
/publicCloudInfo/100

blocks.text: A successful response returns code 204. To learn more, see API Response Codes and Error Messages.
The following table provides details of additional AWS APIs that you can use to perform various operations:

table: Retrieve a list of AWS supported regions
Send a GET request to /publicCloudInfo/supportedRegions. The GET request retrieves details such as cloud type, region ID, and region name.
Retrieve the total number of AWS accounts.
Create an external ID for an AWS account.
Retrieve basic information about the AWS cloud accounts.
Enable or disable a specific AWS account in all regions based on the provided ID.
Send a PUT request to /publicCloudInfo/{id}/changeState. Provide AWS account ID and enable (True) or disable (False) in the request payload.
Send a GET request to publicCloudInfo/cloudFormationTemplate.
